projects.name: CANOPY: Adaptive-Granularity Evidence Compression for Multimodal RAG
projects.problem: Choosing a retrieval granularity does not settle how much of each retrieved item to keep: coarse units carry irrelevant content, uniformly fine selection strips the context needed to interpret the evidence, and existing compressors handle the trade-off per modality.
projects.contribution: Represented retrieved items as hierarchies and scored regions against the query with a node encoder trained on gold evidence, selecting several granularities at once by parent-relative refinement with no LLM calls for node-level pruning; across five QA benchmarks over a 33M-item heterogeneous corpus, cut reader-input evidence tokens by 14.2–27.7% at comparable accuracy.

projects.name: Hi-Q: Hierarchical Evidence-guided Query Refinement for Multi-Hop Question Answering
projects.problem: A question is phrased at one granularity while the corpus is retrievable at another. Prior work imposes a fixed graph over the corpus, reformulates the query, or runs a generated program, but none decides when a query unit is already supported by evidence and when it must be refined.
projects.contribution: Posed this as retrievable granularity discovery: a resolution operator tests each query node against retrieved evidence, resolved nodes terminate, and unresolved ones expand through a dependency-preserving binary operator checked by a semantic coverage verifier — 52.3 EM / 64.0 F1 averaged over three multi-hop QA benchmarks under full-corpus retrieval, 15.1 EM over IRCoT.

projects.name: SPARTA: Scalable and Principled Benchmark of Tree-Structured Multi-hop QA over Text and Tables
projects.problem: Multi-hop QA benchmarks spanning text and tables are expensive to annotate, and existing ones give no guarantee that a generated query is answerable or that its structure looks natural.
projects.contribution: Built a fully automated SQL-centric pipeline that unifies tables and text into one relational representation, with provenance-based refinement for query validity and realistic-structure enforcement for phrasing — a quarter of HybridQA's annotation time.

projects.name: Home AI Agent with Event Memory
projects.event: Korean government-hosted AI competition — finalist (top 20 of 1,100+ teams)
projects.problem: Home cameras emit a stream of near-identical observations, so recovering what happened earlier means replaying footage, and recency-ordered logs bury the state changes that matter.
projects.contribution: Built event memory that merges continuing scenes into events while preserving observation counts and state transitions — 72 observations into 6 events (91.7% fewer list entries), and cited the designated event in 6 of 7 past-event questions against 3 for a recent-3-records baseline.

projects.name: Life-Event-Based Public Service AI Agent
projects.event: Korean government-hosted AI competition — finalist (top 20 of 1,100+ teams)
projects.problem: Public services are indexed by procedure name, so residents who only know their own situation cannot tell what to file; and because procedures span multiple steps and deadlines, an agent that does not retain their conditions and completed steps forces them to re-explain each time.
projects.contribution: Kept the user's conditions and completion state as persistent memory and used it to decide what to surface next; linked 806 procedure items across 50 life events by 639 precedence relations, cutting precedence violations from 242 under deadline-only ordering to 0 on a 500-case regression.
